remarks: Every *.wb.gov.in and *.wblabour.gov.in host tried (silpasathi.wb.gov.in, labour.wb.gov.in, www.labour.wb.gov.in, wb.gov.in, lc.wb.gov.in, bmssy.wblabour.gov.in, comtax.wb.gov.in) failed identically with a TLS-handshake-level connection reset ('Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' right after Client Hello) across 15+ attempts and multiple retries spaced several minutes apart, while unrelated .gov.in domains (dgfasli.gov.in, indiacode.nic.in homepage, nsws.gov.in, india.gov.in) and other West Bengal domains that are NOT on the wb.gov.in suffix (wbidc.com, paschimmedinipur.gov.in) all resolved fine with HTTP 200 in the same session. This points to the wb.gov.in domain family itself being unreachable from this session's egress path (not generic proxy congestion, and not a problem specific to any one candidate URL) — the agent-proxy status endpoint also logged these as 'ws_closed_mid_exchange' on the relay side. This is also the single-window portal (Silpasathi/Silpa Sathi) that is the actual official route for obtaining a Factory License in West Bengal, so the most load-bearing primary source could not be verified this session despite being the right target.

Because the Silpasathi portal itself was unreachable, verifiedSources instead relies on (a) WBIDC (wbidc.com, a non-wb.gov.in domain) pages that independently and explicitly list 'Factory License under Factories Act 1948' as a required approval and name the Directorate of Factories as issuing authority, (b) a central DGFASLI (Ministry of Labour & Employment) PDF confirming the West Bengal factory-inspectorate contact, and (c) a district-government (NIC-hosted, non-wb.gov.in-suffix) page describing the Silpasathi scheme and application process. None of these are a substitute for fetching the Silpasathi portal and its official checklist/manual PDFs directly, which should be retried in a later session/environment where wb.gov.in is reachable.

No West Bengal-specific National Single Window System (NSWS, nsws.gov.in) page was found or included: WebSearch results and the WBIDC/Silpasathi material consistently indicate West Bengal routes factory licensing through its own state single-window system (Silpasathi, under the West Bengal Single Window System Act, 2017) rather than through the central NSWS platform, so NSWS was not treated as directly relevant to this state's FAL process.

Several non-government aggregator/consultancy sources (IndiaFilings, Professional Utilities, WikiProcedure, Greythr, Indian Kanoon, ksandk.com, lexplosion.in, Simpliance, PRS Legislative Research) surfaced useful leads in WebSearch (e.g. document checklists, the West Bengal Factories Rules 1958 text, the West Bengal Single Window System Act 2017 PDF) but were deliberately excluded from both verifiedSources and excluded per the spec's rule against non-government sources, even though some appear accurate.
